Title: October 1, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Meeting (Regular Meeting with Public Hearing on 2027 Budget)

Topic1.Title: Amend agenda and open comment
Topic1.Summary: Council voted to add item 8A on the front range passenger rail sales tax measure to the agenda. Elisha reviewed the public participation guidelines and rules of decorum for open comment. Nineteen people signed up to speak with two-minute limits.

Topic2.Title: Open comment on federal, housing, tenant, and development concerns
Topic2.Summary: Residents spoke on a range of issues including a request for council to respond to federal actions, tenant union formation, Boulderthon road closures, unpermitted small cell towers near Boulder Meadows, Belmont property hazards, and CU South and Gunbarrel parks and safety. Speakers also raised concerns about Spruce Pool, a proposed botanic garden at Hogan Pancost, and the East Boulder Rec Center. Staff and council responded to several comments.

Topic3.Title: Consent agenda
Topic3.Summary: Council approved consent agenda items 3A through 3H unanimously after a motion and second with no questions raised.

Topic4.Title: Call-up check-in for Nuropa campus site review
Topic4.Summary: Council reviewed a site review application to redevelop the Nuropa campus with about 135 residential units and a height modification to four stories and 55 feet. Council Member Winer raised shadow and setback concerns, and the applicant responded that setbacks exceed 40 feet and solar analysis met city standards. No member called the item up.

Topic5.Title: Public hearing on 2027 recommended budget and ordinances
Topic5.Summary: Staff presented the 2027 recommended budget totaling about 552.6 million, with a 2.35 percent operating budget increase and a 135.4 million capital budget. Highlights included wildfire funding of about 10.9 million, three new police lieutenants, affordable housing investments, and a proposed Spruce Pool operations reduction. Council discussed wildfire funding timing ahead of the October 22 study session and the relationship to open space funds.

Topic6.Title: Council proposals to hold or realign wildfire funding
Topic6.Summary: Council Member Benjamin proposed holding about 2.5 million for wildfire mitigation, while Council Member Kaplan proposed holding 600,000. Staff noted the funding source would need to be identified and that realignment could occur through the adjustment-to-base process. Straw polls did not reach a majority, so the budget proceeded without these changes and council planned to revisit wildfire funding after the October 22 study session.

Topic7.Title: Council proposal to reallocate police funds to behavioral health response
Topic7.Summary: Council Member Tisha proposed redirecting part of police funding toward partnerships for mental health and behavioral response to non-emergency calls. Housing and Human Services staff explained that the care program was restructured because of low call volumes and would relaunch with clinicians and case managers. Council Member Tisha withdrew the amendment after the explanation.

Topic8.Title: Adoption of 2027 budget ordinances
Topic8.Summary: Council voted on four ordinances: adopting the 2027 budget (7-1 with Adams opposed), setting property mill levies for 2026 (unanimous), appropriating funds for 2027 (unanimous), and amending fees and taxes in the Boulder Revised Code (7-1 with Adams opposed). Several members made closing remarks about budget process, staff work, and the need for a longer-term budget cycle.

Topic9.Title: Straw poll supporting Front Range passenger rail sales tax measure
Topic9.Summary: Council Member Winer asked council whether to take a position of support on the Front Range passenger rail sales tax measure. The straw poll was unanimous, directing staff to prepare a resolution of support for a future business meeting.
